about.title: Simi Valley Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Simi Valley takes many shapes: warehouse and light-industrial shifts off Los Angeles Avenue, retail and restaurant jobs along Cochran Street, construction and maintenance crews spread across Ventura County, and delivery routes that run the length of SR-118. When something goes wrong on the clock, the first question is usually where the money for care and lost wages will come from. In California, workers' compensation is normally the exclusive remedy against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. That is not always the whole picture, though. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the harm, a separate injury claim against that third party may be available alongside your comp benefits. Public records logged 357 injury collisions in Simi Valley in 2025, with 500 people hurt, and some of those involved people driving for work. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to you, and every attorney in our network works on contingency.

items.title: We Look Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver can be a separate defendant. The attorneys we connect you with know how to spot that second path.

items.title: Deadlines Are Different for Each Claim
items.desc: You generally need to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, while a third-party injury claim carries a two-year filing deadline. An attorney can keep both clocks straight so nothing lapses.

items.title: Free Connection, No Fee Without Recovery
items.desc: LawProactive charges you nothing to make the match, and network attorneys work on contingency. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee.

items.question: I was hit on SR-118 while making deliveries for my employer. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of fault. Separately, if the other driver was negligent, you may have a third-party injury claim against that driver with its own two-year deadline. An attorney can evaluate how the two claims interact.

items.question: Can my Simi Valley employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. You should still report the injury to your employer as soon as you can, ideally within 30 days, so your benefits are not put at risk. If you believe you have faced retaliation, mention it when you speak with an attorney.

items.question: Do I need a lawyer if workers' comp is already paying my bills?
items.answer: Not always, but it is worth a conversation. Comp benefits are limited and do not cover things like pain and suffering, while a claim against a negligent third party can. An independent attorney can tell you whether anyone other than your employer may share responsibility, and the initial connection through LawProactive costs you nothing.
